summary.allegation: The issuer states the cardholder did not authorise the 29 April 2025 charge of GBP 87.40 at QuickStream Digital, that the card was in the cardholder's possession, and that the cardholder has no relationship with the merchant.
summary.to_defend: Mastercard requires any two of: full AVS plus CVV match, successful 3D Secure authentication, two prior undisputed transactions with matching billing details, or signed proof of delivery to the billing address.

requirements.title: AVS and CVV match
requirements.text: AVS match (full address) AND CVV match on the disputed transaction.
requirements.finding: Transaction metadata shows avs_result N and cvv_result N, so neither the address nor the security code matched at authorisation.
requirements.gap: Both AVS and CVV failed at authorisation; no matching verification exists for this transaction.

requirements.title: 3DS authenticated
requirements.text: 3D Secure authentication completed successfully (Mastercard SecureCode / Identity Check).
requirements.finding: Transaction metadata records three_ds_status as not_attempted, so no Mastercard Identity Check authentication was performed.
requirements.gap: No 3D Secure authentication was attempted at the time of the transaction and this cannot be created after the fact.

requirements.title: Two prior undisputed transactions
requirements.text: Two prior undisputed transactions from the same cardholder with this merchant in the past 12 months, with matching billing details.
requirements.finding: The merchant's own report describes the customer account age as new and first transaction, with 24h velocity of one transaction, so there are no two prior undisputed transactions.
requirements.gap: No prior transaction history with this cardholder exists; the merchant's own record states this was the first transaction.

requirements.title: Signed delivery to billing address
requirements.text: Proof of delivery to the cardholder's billing address with signature.
requirements.finding: This is an MCC 5815 digital media purchase with no shipping address recorded in the transaction metadata, so no physical delivery with signature could have occurred.

documents.label: Merchant internal fraud screening report
documents.reason: An internal risk score generated on 12 May 2025 does not evidence AVS/CVV match, 3D Secure, prior transaction history or delivery, and it confirms this was the customer's first transaction.

alerts.text: D1 concludes the transaction passed fraud screening and is legitimate, but it omits that AVS and CVV both returned N and 3D Secure was not attempted per the transaction metadata; the analyst should rely on the authorisation data, not the internal score.

reasons: Every requirement the decision relies on is backed by verified evidence

checks.label: No requirement is partly met, so accepting isn't borderline
Key evidence comes from document text, not only from an image
Images the evidence relies on are fully legible
Every quoted passage was found in the documents
The disputed charge matches the merchant's own records
The rule check and the AI recommendation agree

justification: Accept liability: with R1 and R2 failed at authorisation and R3 contradicted by the merchant's own record of a first-time customer, the two-requirement threshold cannot be met and R4 cannot apply to this digital MCC 5815 sale.
rationale:
The cardholder denies authorising the GBP 87.40 charge of 29 April 2025 (txn_7762GH) at QuickStream Digital.
Authorisation data shows AVS result N and CVV result N, so neither the billing address nor the security code matched.
3D Secure was not attempted, so there is no Identity Check authentication to rely on.
The merchant's own screening report records the customer account as new with this as the first transaction, so there is no prior undisputed transaction history, and no goods were shipped for this digital MCC 5815 purchase.
The Mastercard compelling evidence threshold cannot be met and liability is accepted.
analyst_notes: Transaction was placed at 03:42 UTC from an unseen device fingerprint and an IP in a high risk range, which supports the fraud claim.
Confirm with the merchant whether any account login or product access logs exist before closing, though they would not satisfy any of the four requirements.
